q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of ERW steel pipe?
title: ERW steel pipe carbon footprint per tonne
short: Start with the hot-rolled coil, which carries most of the footprint, using the steel supplier's figure per tonne. Add slitting, forming, welding, galvanising if any and finishing energy, then divide the mill's energy by tonnes of pipe dispatched.

ul: Hot-rolled steel coil, the main input.
Zinc if the pipe is galvanised.
Paint or varnish for black pipe.
Slitting the coil and roll forming the tube.
Hydro testing, cutting and end finishing.

p: Report per tonne by size and finish. Galvanised pipe adds the zinc and the galvanising bath to the black pipe figure.

example.title: Worked example: plant energy per tonne (one month)
lines: Plant total: 218,500 / 5,000 = 43.7 kg CO2 per tonne
Add hot-rolled coil and any zinc for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
